title: A cartesian line presentation agrees with Zariski restriction
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], $P$ a coherent etale line presentation [def-trf-cartesian-line-presentation], and $W\to X$ any representable etale scheme test. The ordinary module $P_W$ is isomorphic to the Zariski restriction of $P.line$ along $W\to X$ [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction]. No section algebra, morphism to a scheme or cover of X is needed.

source.place: Tag 03G7, restriction to scheme tests; descent.tex Tags 03DX and 03FH.

proof.text: For every open V of W, tensorOpenSectionIso identifies sections of P_W on V with global sections of its tensor pullback to V. The cartesian family comparison and P.etaleSections identify these with the sections of P.line on the open-subscheme test V.

The comparisons are additive and linear over regular functions. Coherence of the family and the unit-normalized open-section comparison identify open restriction with sectionMap. P.etaleSections_naturality then gives naturality on all open inclusions. Assemble the pointwise linear equivalences and their inverses into mutually inverse module-sheaf morphisms.
